task.description: WF-03 Step 4b: independently verify TEST-DESIGNER's coverage of design doc iss0389-advance-timer-endpoint.md AC1-AC10 and the full-suite/mutation claims.

result.summary: Coverage gap on AC3. Design doc §6 AC3 requires four specific role_allows? assertions for :InstancesAdvanceTimer: PROCESS_OPERATOR==true, TASK_WORKER==false, AGENT_RUNNER==false, PLATFORM_ADMIN==true. Cross-referenced every test in the diff (test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs, test/letflow/api/authorization_enforcement_test.exs, test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs 'advance-timer' describe block): PROCESS_OPERATOR==true is exercised indirectly (AC5's 200 test uses roles: ['PROCESS_OPERATOR']), TASK_WORKER==false is exercised indirectly (the dedicated 403 test uses roles: ['TASK_WORKER']). AGENT_RUNNER and PLATFORM_ADMIN are NOT referenced anywhere in the diff in connection with :InstancesAdvanceTimer or advance-timer -- no unit test in authorization_test.exs's 'PROCESS_OPERATOR grants InstancesCancel...'-style per-role grant/deny pattern was added for this permission, and no router-level test uses PLATFORM_ADMIN or AGENT_RUNNER against the advance-timer route. This is a real, mechanically-identifiable coverage gap, not a style nitpick: AC3 is a closed four-assertion criterion and two of the four have zero test coverage anywhere in the suite.
other_checks_performed: AC1: verified by grep -n 'advance-timer' lib/letflow/routers/instances.ex (route present) -- not itself asserted by a test, but this is the router's own registration; AC4's route-walk test in authorization_enforcement_test.exs mechanically confirms endpoint_policy_key('POST','/instances/:id/advance-timer') resolves to the exact declared key :InstancesAdvanceTimer (real_key == declared_key branch) with no @allowlist entry needed -- AC2's first clause and AC4 are both genuinely covered.

AC2 second clause (required_permission(:InstancesAdvanceTimer) == :InstancesAdvanceTimer) has no standalone unit assertion, but is exercised transitively by every router-level advance-timer test (the full authz pipeline runs it) -- acceptable as coverage, same standard as AC3's PROCESS_OPERATOR/TASK_WORKER paths.

AC5-AC9: each has a direct, well-isolated router-level test in test/letflow/routers/instances_test.exs 'advance-timer' describe block, including negative-state assertions (timers remain pending on 400/404/422/403). Confirmed adequate.

AC10: confirmed correctly handled -- the stale absence-check test was removed (not left red), following this file's own established 'SUPERSEDED by <ISS/REQ>' comment convention used elsewhere in the same file for an analogous REQ-212 case. Adequate.
resolve_advance_target/3: all 7 design-specified branches (scheduler_test.exs's two new describe blocks) are each independently covered by an isolated test. Adequate.

Fixture scope judgment (process_shipment_dispatch.yaml TIMER node + injury-check-merge gateway, req206_swiftroute_test.exs definition-key fix): read both diffs in full. Verdict: genuinely necessary, not scope creep. Un-skipping step 2 (mandated by this issue's own AC5/AC10) requires actually dispatching this fixture through Engine.create/2 for the first time ever; the wrong-definition-key bug and the combined_split_join_not_supported gateway bug both block that dispatch outright (Engine.create/2 would reject the graph, and the test would exercise the wrong process entirely) -- these are not optional cleanups, the scenario literally cannot run without both fixes. Documented inline with clear header comments in both files rather than silently glossed over. No objection.

Spec shape (test/specs/ISS-0389.md) compared against test/specs/REQ-156.md: comparable structure and rigor (change summary, per-file test-case breakdown, mutation-check section, verification-performed with real command output, coverage checklist). Adequate.

Full-suite claim (444/446) and the mutation-test claim (80->78->80) were NOT independently re-run: this sandbox has no mix/elixir/erl on PATH at all (confirmed: `command -v mix elixir erl` all empty) -- no toolchain available to execute mix test or apply/revert a mutant myself. Flagging per core-directives 'if you can't run it, say so explicitly instead of guessing' rather than passing on the strength of TEST-DESIGNER's report. This must still be independently confirmed (by re-running in an environment with the toolchain) before this proceeds, in addition to the AC3 fix below.
required_fix: Add explicit role_allows? coverage for :InstancesAdvanceTimer covering all four roles named in design AC3 (PROCESS_OPERATOR=true, TASK_WORKER=false, AGENT_RUNNER=false, PLATFORM_ADMIN=true) -- either as a dedicated unit test in test/letflow/api/authorization_test.exs matching that file's existing 'X grants Y, denies Z' per-role pattern, or as explicit router-level tests exercising PLATFORM_ADMIN (200) and AGENT_RUNNER (403) against POST .../advance-timer alongside the existing PROCESS_OPERATOR/TASK_WORKER cases. Either location is acceptable; leaving AGENT_RUNNER and PLATFORM_ADMIN untested for this permission is not.

When resubmitting, re-confirm (with a toolchain available) that mix letflow.check.test's real total and the mutation-test result match what was reported -- this validator could not execute mix in this sandbox and the claim remains unverified pending an environment where it can be re-run.
